steps.title: Import TypeScript and define plugin lifecycle event types
steps.instruction: Create type definitions for plugin lifecycle events: initialize, beforeMount, afterMount, beforeUnmount, and afterUnmount.
steps.hint: Use the TypeScript 'type' keyword to define a union type containing the five lifecycle event strings.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: defining a type for status values
type Status = 'pending' | 'active' | 'completed';

steps.expectedOutcome: A TypeScript type definition that includes all five lifecycle event strings as union members.
successCriteria: A type named PluginLifecycleEvent is defined with the five required event strings as union members.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the PluginLifecycleEvent type with all required lifecycle events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but make sure your type includes all five lifecycle events: initialize, beforeMount, afterMount, beforeUnmount, and afterUnmount.
steps.feedbackWrong: The type definition is missing or incorrect. Create a type named PluginLifecycleEvent that includes all five lifecycle event strings.

steps.title: Define the Plugin interface with lifecycle methods
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface named 'Plugin' that includes optional lifecycle methods: 'onInit', 'onMount', and 'onUnmount', each typed as functions that return void.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name, then define the methods with optional '?' modifier and proper function type signatures.
steps.seedCode:
// Define your plugin lifecycle event types here

// Define the Plugin interface below
steps.expectedOutcome: A Plugin interface is defined with optional lifecycle methods matching the event types from step 1.
successCriteria: The Plugin interface is defined with optional onInit, onMount, and onUnmount methods that return void.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Plugin interface with the required lifecycle methods.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure all three methods (onInit, onMount, onUnmount) are optional and return void.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Plugin interface definition is missing or incorrect. Check that you've defined an interface with optional lifecycle methods.

steps.title: Create the PluginHook interface for managing plugins
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named PluginHook with methods to manage plugin lifecycle. Define a method to register plugins and another to trigger lifecycle events.
steps.hint: Think of PluginHook as a manager that will handle plugin registration and lifecycle event triggering. Use the Plugin interface you defined earlier as a parameter type.
steps.expectedOutcome: A PluginHook interface with registerPlugin and triggerLifecycleEvent methods is added to the code.
successCriteria: The PluginHook interface is defined with registerPlugin and triggerLifecycleEvent methods using proper TypeScript syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the PluginHook interface with the required methods for managing plugin lifecycle.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the PluginHook interface, but make sure to include both registerPlugin and triggerLifecycleEvent methods with proper TypeScript signatures.
steps.feedbackWrong: The PluginHook interface is missing or incorrect. Create an interface named PluginHook with methods to register plugins and trigger lifecycle events.

steps.title: Implement the createPluginHook function
steps.instruction: Create a function named createPluginHook that returns a PluginHook implementation. The function should take no parameters and return an object matching the PluginHook interface.
steps.hint: Define a function that returns an object with the properties defined in the PluginHook interface (plugins, register, unregister, trigger). You can initialize plugins as an empty array.
steps.expectedOutcome: A createPluginHook function is implemented that returns a PluginHook object with the required methods and properties.
successCriteria: The createPluginHook function is defined and returns an object with plugins array, register, unregister, and trigger methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the createPluginHook factory function that returns a typed plugin hook instance.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function returns an object with all the properties defined in the PluginHook interface.
steps.feedbackWrong: The createPluginHook function is not properly implemented. It should return an object matching the PluginHook interface structure.

steps.title: Initialize the plugins array in createPluginHook
steps.instruction: Inside the createPluginHook function, declare a private plugins array variable to store registered plugins. Initialize it as an empty array.
steps.hint: You need to create a variable inside the function closure. Use the Plugin interface type for the array elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createPluginHook function now has a private plugins array variable that will store registered plugin instances.
successCriteria: A plugins array variable is declared inside createPluginHook and initialized as an empty array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the plugins array. This private array will store all registered plugins within the hook's closure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared the plugins array variable inside the createPluginHook function and initialized it as an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The plugins array needs to be declared inside the createPluginHook function. Try adding a variable like 'plugins' and setting it to an empty array.

steps.title: Implement the registerPlugin method
steps.instruction: Inside the createPluginHook function, add a registerPlugin method that takes a Plugin parameter and pushes it to the plugins array.
steps.hint: The method should be part of the returned object and have a signature like registerPlugin(plugin: Plugin): void.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createPluginHook function now returns an object with a registerPlugin method that can add plugins to the internal array.
successCriteria: The registerPlugin method is defined inside the returned object, accepts a Plugin parameter, and pushes it to the plugins array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the typed registerPlugin method. This allows plugins to be added to your hook system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure registerPlugin is a method in the returned object that takes a Plugin parameter and pushes it to the plugins array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The registerPlugin method isn't implemented correctly. It should be inside the returned object and add plugins to the array.

steps.title: Create the triggerLifecycleEvent helper function
steps.instruction: Inside the createPluginHook function, create a helper function named triggerLifecycleEvent that takes an eventName parameter of type string and returns void.
steps.hint: Define a function that will iterate through plugins and call their lifecycle methods. Start by declaring the function signature.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createPluginHook function now contains a triggerLifecycleEvent helper function declaration with proper TypeScript typing.
successCriteria: A function named triggerLifecycleEvent is defined inside createPluginHook with a string parameter eventName and void return type.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the triggerLifecycleEvent helper function with proper TypeScript typing. This function will be used to execute lifecycle methods on all registered plugins.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but check the name, parameter type, or return type. Make sure it's named triggerLifecycleEvent, takes a string parameter called eventName, and returns void.
steps.feedbackWrong: The triggerLifecycleEvent helper function is not properly defined. Create a function inside createPluginHook with the correct signature.

steps.title: Implement the initialize method
steps.instruction: Inside the createPluginHook function, add an initialize method to the returned object that calls triggerLifecycleEvent with 'initialize' as the event name.
steps.hint: The method should be a function that triggers the 'initialize' lifecycle event on all registered plugins.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createPluginHook function now returns an object with an initialize method that will trigger the initialize lifecycle event.
successCriteria: The initialize method is defined in the returned object and calls triggerLifecycleEvent with 'initialize'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the initialize method that will trigger the initialize lifecycle event on all registered plugins.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the initialize method properly calls triggerLifecycleEvent with 'initialize' as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The initialize method is missing or doesn't call triggerLifecycleEvent with 'initialize'. Review the expected implementation.

steps.title: Implement the mount method
steps.instruction: Inside the createPluginHook function, add a mount method to the returned object that triggers the 'beforeMount' lifecycle event, performs mount logic, then triggers the 'afterMount' event.
steps.hint: The mount method should call triggerLifecycleEvent with 'beforeMount', then execute mount logic (like logging), then call triggerLifecycleEvent with 'afterMount'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createPluginHook function now returns an object with a mount method that will execute lifecycle events in the correct order.
successCriteria: The mount method triggers 'beforeMount', performs mount logic (like console.log), then triggers 'afterMount'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the mount method with proper lifecycle event sequencing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the mount method, but make sure it calls triggerLifecycleEvent for both 'beforeMount' and 'afterMount' with mount logic in between.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mount method is missing or doesn't follow the required sequence. It should trigger 'beforeMount', execute mount logic, then trigger 'afterMount'.

steps.title: Implement the unmount method
steps.instruction: Inside the createPluginHook function, add an unmount method to the returned object that triggers the 'beforeUnmount' lifecycle event, performs unmount logic, then triggers the 'afterUnmount' event.
steps.hint: Follow the same pattern as the initialize and mount methods: call triggerLifecycleEvent with the appropriate event name, then add your unmount logic (like clearing resources), then trigger the next event.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createPluginHook function now returns an object with an unmount method that will execute the unmount lifecycle sequence.
successCriteria: The unmount method exists in the returned object and contains calls to triggerLifecycleEvent for 'beforeUnmount' and 'afterUnmount' events with unmount logic in between.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the unmount method with proper lifecycle event sequencing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the unmount method, but make sure it triggers both 'beforeUnmount' and 'afterUnmount' events with unmount logic in between.
steps.feedbackWrong: The unmount method is missing or doesn't follow the correct lifecycle pattern. It should trigger 'beforeUnmount', perform unmount logic, then trigger 'afterUnmount'.

steps.title: Create a sample plugin implementation
steps.instruction: Create a LoggerPlugin class that implements the Plugin interface with lifecycle methods that log to console.
steps.hint: Define a class named LoggerPlugin that implements Plugin. Add the required lifecycle methods (initialize, mount, unmount) that each log a message to console.
steps.expectedOutcome: A LoggerPlugin class is created that implements the Plugin interface with console logging in each lifecycle method.
successCriteria: LoggerPlugin class exists, implements Plugin, and has initialize, mount, and unmount methods that each log a message to console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a concrete plugin implementation that logs to console during each lifecycle event.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure LoggerPlugin implements the Plugin interface and all three lifecycle methods (initialize, mount, unmount) log messages to console.
steps.feedbackWrong: The LoggerPlugin class is missing or doesn't properly implement the Plugin interface with logging lifecycle methods.

steps.title: Test the plugin hook system with the sample plugin
steps.instruction: Create a plugin hook instance, register the LoggerPlugin, and call its initialize, mount, and unmount methods to test the lifecycle events.
steps.hint: Instantiate the plugin hook using createPluginHook(), then call registerPlugin with a new LoggerPlugin instance. Finally, call each lifecycle method in sequence.
steps.expectedOutcome: The plugin hook system will be tested by creating an instance, registering the LoggerPlugin, and triggering all lifecycle events in sequence.
successCriteria: A plugin hook instance is created, LoggerPlugin is registered, and initialize, mount, and unmount methods are called.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully tested the typed plugin hook system with lifecycle events.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you create the hook instance, register the LoggerPlugin, and call all three lifecycle methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you're creating the plugin hook instance, registering LoggerPlugin, and calling initialize, mount, and unmount methods.
